<!--
WHAT THIS FIGURE IS FOR

The `stall_reads >= 10` floor (gate G1; the rank plots need it reapplied at plot time) is currently
justified by argument: at 1-2 reads a stall fraction can be 1.000 and mean nothing. The
relationship it corrects for has never been plotted. This figure shows it, so the threshold is
visible rather than asserted, and so that any single site's SF can be read against what sites at
comparable depth actually give.

WHICH SET IS DRAWN, AND WHY IT MATTERS. `peaks_annotated.csv` retains EVERY candidate row
regardless of the v7.3 gates; `sites.csv` is the gated set. The rank plots draw their grey "all"
background from the annotated file, which is why both rank plots need the floor reapplied. This notebook reads the annotated
file deliberately -- the ungated rows ARE the subject -- and marks the gate boundaries rather
than filtering them away.

ONE NOTEBOOK, BOTH LIBRARIES. Set LIB below and knit twice.

INPUTS: the per-condition peaks_annotated.csv, copied down from the cluster into the figure's
inputs/ directory. Nothing is recomputed here.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, dev = "cairo_pdf")
library(tidyverse); library(scales); library(patchwork)

# Every plot chunk is saved as both .svg and .pdf as well as rendering inline, to
# plots/<chunk_label>.{svg,pdf}. Same convention as zero_pass_wellpowered_distribution.Rmd.
FIG_DIR <- "plots"
dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)

save_plot <- function(plot, label, width = 11, height = 4.2) {
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(label, ".svg")), plot = plot,
         width = width, height = height, device = "svg")
  ggsave(file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(label, ".pdf")), plot = plot,
         width = width, height = height, device = "pdf")
}
```

```{r config}
# ---- THE ONLY THING TO CHANGE BETWEEN THE TWO KNITS -------------------------------------
LIB <- "flaviLib"          # "flaviLib" or "viromelib"

CFG <- list(
  flaviLib = list(
    base       = "~/Desktop/viromelib/flaviLib/figures/sf_vs_depth",
    tables     = c("10mM" = "261021_flaviLib_150x150_10mM.peaks_annotated.csv",
                   "01mM" = "261021_flaviLib_150x150_01mM.peaks_annotated.csv"),
    n_reps     = 4,
    min_reps   = 2,
    gate_label = "2 of 4 replicates"
  ),
  viromelib = list(
    base       = "~/Desktop/viromelib/figures/sf_vs_depth",
    tables     = c("X" = "261019_orderedRef_peaks_annotated.csv"),
    n_reps     = 3,
    min_reps   = 2,
    gate_label = "2 of 3 replicates"
  )
)[[LIB]]

# v7.3 gates, for the reference lines. Not applied -- drawn.
GATE <- list(stall_reads = 10, treated_sf = 0.3, qvalue = 0.01)

# The gate panels D/E call "passing", and the one the reading notes were measured under.
# Deliberately NOT the v7.3 qvalue: 0.05 with 3 of 4 replicates is the stricter replicate
# requirement, and it is what produced the 38-read effective floor recorded below.
FIG <- list(qvalue = 0.05, min_reps = 3)

# Sites to mark individually. Leave empty for the general figure; fill in to interrogate a
# specific candidate. accession is the BARE accession, pos the genomic stall position.
HIGHLIGHT <- tribble(
  ~label,              ~accession,   ~pos,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "NC_001809",  10765,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "NC_003687",  10734,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "NC_003690",  10838,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "NC_001672",  11036,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "NC_027709",  10764,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "NC_005062",  10681,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "MN830233",   10711,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "MH688511",   10680,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "KT224356",   10874,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "JF416957",   10667,
  "cand_FJTB_261026",  "JF416967",   10641
)
```

```{r load}
read_one <- function(cond, fn) {
  read_csv(file.path(CFG$base, "inputs", fn), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(condition = cond)
}
raw <- imap_dfr(CFG$tables, ~ read_one(.y, .x))

rep_cols <- function(prefix) paste0(prefix, "_R", seq_len(CFG$n_reps))

d <- raw |>
  mutate(
    accession_bare = str_replace(str_split_i(accession, fixed("|"), 1), "\\.\\d+$", ""),
    pos            = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(stall_site_genomic_position)),
    # Summed treated stall reads across replicates. The alternative -- the best replicate -- is
    # more charitable; summed is what detectability_floor.py uses, so keep it consistent and say so.
    stall_reads    = rowSums(across(any_of(rep_cols("stall_reads_treated"))), na.rm = TRUE),
    sf             = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(median_treated_sf)),
    # median_treated_sf is the median across ALL replicates, including ones that failed their
    # own peak gate. sf_pass is the median over passing replicates only. Measured 2026-10-28:
    # the two differ only for n_reps_passing == 3 rows (by construction), and the 10 mM median
    # there rises 0.343 -> 0.368. The larger effect is compositional, see sf_by_reps below.

    q              = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(meta_qvalue)),
    pval           = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(meta_pvalue)),
    reps_passing   = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(n_reps_passing))
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(sf), !is.na(stall_reads), stall_reads > 0)

# SF over PASSING replicates only. peak_pass_R* is written by Python as True/False, which readr
# may read as character, so compare on the uppercased string rather than relying on the parse.
sf_m <- as.matrix(d[, rep_cols("treated_sf")])
pp_m <- as.matrix(d[, rep_cols("peak_pass")])
storage.mode(sf_m) <- "double"
sf_m[toupper(trimws(as.character(pp_m))) != "TRUE"] <- NA_real_
d$sf_pass <- apply(sf_m, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
d$sf_pass[!is.finite(d$sf_pass)] <- NA_real_

# CM class per row, from whichever *.cm_hit column is non-NA. A row can carry more than one;
# label those "multiple" rather than silently taking the first (decision 28).
hit_cols <- names(d)[str_detect(names(d), "\\.cm_hit$")]
HAS_CM <- length(hit_cols) > 0
# Defensive only. The 261021 tables DO carry all seven models' columns plus any_hit (91 columns);
# an earlier note here claiming otherwise was wrong.
if (!HAS_CM) warning("no *.cm_hit columns in these tables -- panel C is skipped.")
cm_short <- function(x) x |>
  str_remove("\\.cm_hit$") |> str_remove("^CL_") |> str_remove("_xrRNA_final") |>
  str_remove("_NAR_2025.*") |> str_remove("_cl4_v9_20260824") |> str_remove("_RF00525")

d <- if (HAS_CM) {
  d |> mutate(n_hits = rowSums(across(all_of(hit_cols), ~ !is.na(.x))),
              cm_class = case_when(
                n_hits == 0 ~ "no hit",
                n_hits  > 1 ~ "multiple",
                TRUE ~ cm_short(hit_cols[apply(across(all_of(hit_cols), ~ !is.na(.x)), 1, which.max)])
              ))
} else {
  d |> mutate(n_hits = NA_integer_, cm_class = NA_character_)
}
d <- d |> mutate(passes = reps_passing >= CFG$min_reps)

# HIGHLIGHT carries its own `pos`, which collides with d$pos on the join and is silently
# suffixed to pos.x / pos.y. Rename before joining so both are addressable by name.
marked <- d |>
  inner_join(HIGHLIGHT |> rename(hl_pos = pos), by = c("accession_bare" = "accession")) |>
  filter(is.na(hl_pos) | abs(pos - hl_pos) <= 3)
```

```{r panelA, fig.height=4.2}
# A. the relationship the floor corrects for
pA <- ggplot(d, aes(stall_reads, sf)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = passes), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = GATE$stall_reads, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = GATE$treated_sf, linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("text", x = GATE$stall_reads, y = 1.04, hjust = -0.1, size = 3,
           label = paste0("G1: stall_reads >= ", GATE$stall_reads)) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = GATE$treated_sf, hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5, size = 3,
           label = paste0("treated SF >= ", GATE$treated_sf)) +
  { if (nrow(marked)) list(
      geom_point(data = marked, colour = "black", size = 1.8, shape = 21, fill = NA, stroke = 0.7),
      ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = marked, aes(label = accession_bare),
                               size = 2.4, max.overlaps = 20, min.segment.length = 0)
    ) } +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey20", `FALSE` = "grey70"),
                      labels = c(`TRUE` = CFG$gate_label, `FALSE` = "below replicate gate"),
                      name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "summed treated stall reads across replicates (log)",
       y = "median treated stall fraction",
       title = "A. Stall fraction against depth, every candidate row",
       subtitle = "peaks_annotated.csv, ungated. The dashed line is the floor the rank plots reapply.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
pA
save_plot(pA, "panelA")
```

```{r panelB, fig.height=4.2}
# B. is SF depth-biased? Binned, so the shape is visible rather than inferred from the cloud.
bins <- c(0, 2, 5, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000, Inf)
pB <- d |>
  mutate(bin = cut(stall_reads, bins, labels = c("1-2","3-5","6-10","11-30","31-100",
                                                 "101-300","301-1k",">1k"))) |>
  filter(!is.na(bin)) |>
  ggplot(aes(bin, sf)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = NA, scale = "width") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.18, outlier.size = 0.3, fill = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = GATE$treated_sf, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "summed treated stall reads", y = "median treated stall fraction",
       title = "B. The same, binned",
       subtitle = "If the leftmost bins sit high, low-depth rows are inflating SF and the floor is doing real work.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
pB
save_plot(pB, "panelB")
```

```{r panelC, fig.height=4.2, eval=HAS_CM}
# C. SF by CM class, WELL-POWERED ROWS ONLY. The class comparison in CMdist-postXrn1.rmd's fig3
# was drawn over all rows; restricting to depth makes it a statement about the elements rather
# than about coverage.
WELL <- 100
pC <- d |>
  filter(stall_reads >= WELL, passes) |>
  mutate(cm_class = fct_reorder(cm_class, sf, .fun = median)) |>
  ggplot(aes(cm_class, sf)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = NA, scale = "width") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.18, outlier.size = 0.3, fill = "white") +
  { if (nrow(marked)) geom_point(
      data = marked |> filter(stall_reads >= WELL, passes),
      colour = "black", size = 1.6, shape = 21, fill = NA, stroke = 0.7) } +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "median treated stall fraction",
       title = paste0("C. Stall fraction by CM class, rows with >= ", WELL, " summed stall reads"),
       subtitle = "Restricted to well-powered, replicate-passing rows, so SF is comparable across classes.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
pC
save_plot(pC, "panelC")
```

```{r depthbins}
# Shared depth bins for panels D and E. Same edges as panel B so the three read together.
BIN_EDGES <- c(0, 2, 5, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000, Inf)
BIN_LABS  <- c("1-2", "3-5", "6-10", "11-30", "31-100", "101-300", "301-1k", ">1k")
d <- d |> mutate(depth_bin = cut(stall_reads, breaks = BIN_EDGES, labels = BIN_LABS))
```

```{r panelD, fig.height=4.2}
# D. The p-value side of the same question. The point is the red line, not the boxes: it is the
# SMALLEST p anywhere in each bin, so it shows what significance a given depth can even reach.
floor_by_bin <- d |> group_by(condition, depth_bin) |>
  summarise(best = suppressWarnings(min(pval, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(is.finite(best))

pD <- ggplot(d, aes(depth_bin, -log10(pmax(pval, 1e-50)))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "grey88", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_line(data = floor_by_bin, aes(depth_bin, -log10(best), group = 1),
            colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = floor_by_bin, aes(depth_bin, -log10(best)),
             colour = "firebrick", size = 1.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey35") +
  facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "summed treated stall reads across replicates",
       y = expression(-log[10] ~ "meta p-value"),
       title = "D. Small p-values are unattainable at low depth",
       subtitle = paste("Red: smallest p observed in the bin. Dashed: p = 0.05.",
                        "A thin row cannot reach significance even when its SF is 1.000.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
pD
save_plot(pD, "panelD")
```

```{r panelE, fig.height=4.2}
# E. Where the GATED set actually lives. The replicate requirement is the operative depth filter;
# G1 sits far below the lowest-depth site that survives it, so raising G1 alone changes nothing.
eff_floor <- d |> filter(q < FIG$qvalue, reps_passing >= FIG$min_reps) |> group_by(condition) |>
  summarise(lo = min(stall_reads), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

pE <- ggplot(d, aes(stall_reads, sf)) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, !(q < FIG$qvalue & reps_passing >= FIG$min_reps)),
             colour = "grey82", size = 0.4) +
  geom_point(data = ~ filter(.x, q < FIG$qvalue, reps_passing >= FIG$min_reps),
             colour = "#1f6fb4", size = 0.7, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = GATE$stall_reads, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_vline(data = eff_floor, aes(xintercept = lo), linetype = "dotted", colour = "#1f6fb4") +
  geom_text(data = eff_floor, aes(x = lo, y = 0.30, label = paste0("lowest passing site: ", lo, " reads")),
            hjust = -0.06, size = 2.6, colour = "#1f6fb4") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_number(big.mark = ",")) +
  facet_wrap(~ condition, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "summed treated stall reads across replicates (log)",
       y = "median treated stall fraction",
       title = "E. The replicate requirement already enforces a far higher floor than G1",
       subtitle = paste0("Blue: q < ", FIG$qvalue, " and >= ", FIG$min_reps, " replicates. Red dashed: G1. ",
                         "Blue dotted: the lowest-depth site that survives the gates.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
pE
save_plot(pE, "panelE")
```

```{r floor_tradeoff, results='asis'}
# What a stricter floor would actually cost, on the gated set.
d |> filter(q < FIG$qvalue, reps_passing >= FIG$min_reps) |> group_by(condition) |>
  group_modify(~ map_dfr(c(10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200, 500), function(T) {
    lost <- .x |> filter(stall_reads < T)
    tibble(threshold = T, n_total = nrow(.x), n_lost = nrow(lost),
           pct_lost = round(100 * nrow(lost) / nrow(.x), 1),
           median_sf_of_lost = round(median(lost$sf), 3))
  })) |> knitr::kable(caption = "Sites lost if the depth floor were raised, gated set only")
```

```{r sf_by_reps, results='asis'}
# Does the all-replicate median skew SF? Two separate questions, answered separately.
cat("\n### SF: all replicates vs passing replicates only\n\n")
d |> filter(q < FIG$qvalue, reps_passing >= FIG$min_reps) |>
  group_by(condition, reps_passing) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `median, all reps`     = round(median(sf, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `median, passing reps` = round(median(sf_pass, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Within a row the two differ only when a replicate failed,",
                               "so only reps_passing < n_reps rows move.")) |> print()

cat("\n### The compositional effect, which is the larger one\n\n")
d |> filter(q < FIG$qvalue, reps_passing >= FIG$min_reps) |>
  group_by(condition, cm_class) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `% at 3 of 4`   = round(100 * mean(reps_passing == 3), 1),
            `median SF`     = round(median(sf, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            `median SF, 4 of 4 only` = round(median(sf[reps_passing == 4], na.rm = TRUE), 3),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(condition, desc(n)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Sites passing 3 of 4 have systematically lower SF than those",
                               "passing 4 of 4, and they are unevenly distributed, so a group",
                               "with more of them looks weaker than it is.")) |> print()
```

```{r numbers, results='asis'}
cat("\n### Numbers quoted in the caption\n\n")
d |> group_by(condition) |>
  summarise(rows = n(),
            `rows below G1` = sum(stall_reads < GATE$stall_reads),
            `SF median, <G1` = round(median(sf[stall_reads <  GATE$stall_reads]), 3),
            `SF median, >=G1` = round(median(sf[stall_reads >= GATE$stall_reads]), 3),
            `SF = 1.000, <G1` = sum(sf == 1 & stall_reads <  GATE$stall_reads),
            `SF = 1.000, >=G1` = sum(sf == 1 & stall_reads >= GATE$stall_reads),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable() |> print()

if (nrow(marked)) {
  cat("\n### Highlighted sites\n\n")
  marked |>
    transmute(condition, label, accession_bare, pos, stall_reads,
              sf = round(sf, 3), q = signif(q, 2), reps_passing, cm_class) |>
    arrange(condition, accession_bare) |>
    knitr::kable() |> print()
}
```

<!--
READING IT -- computed on the 261021 tables 2026-10-27, so the expected shape is known

Panel B: SF is NOT inflated at low depth. Median SF by bin at 10 mM runs
  1-2: 0.043 | 3-5: 0.042 | 6-10: 0.043 | 11-30: 0.049 | 31-100: 0.056
  101-300: 0.070 | 301-1k: 0.106 | >1k: 0.515
flat below the floor and climbing with depth, because a real stall accumulates reads and
fraction together. The SF = 1.000 artefact is narrow, not systematic: 215 rows of 7,531 in the
1-2 bin at 10 mM (256 of 8,818 at 1 mM), and 3 rows above the floor. So reapplying the floor on both rank plots is justified by
removing those specific rows, NOT by a general low-depth bias -- the tracker's wording
("at 1-2 reads SF can be 1.000 and means nothing") describes 2.6 % of that bin.

Panel C, same date, reads >= 100 and reps >= 2, 10 mM / 1 mM medians:
  dumbbell 0.379 / 0.401 | cl3 0.448 / - | no hit 0.449 / 0.435 | Class_2 0.459 / 0.397
  class1c 0.693 / 0.710  | Class_1b 0.720 / 0.737 | Class_1a 0.766 / 0.809
Class 2 is indistinguishable from `no hit` and far below class 1a/1b/1c. So an SF near 0.45 is
NOT weak evidence for a candidate -- it is what class 2 gives. Judge a candidate against the
class its host genomes carry, not against class 1a.

885 well-powered replicate-passing `no hit` sites at median SF 0.449 (10 mM), 415 at 1 mM.

Panel C answers "is this site's SF normal for its class". Restricting to >= 100 summed reads
matters: `CMdist-postXrn1.rmd`'s fig3 drew SF by class over all rows, so a class with many
thin rows looked different from one with few.

Panels D and E, added 2026-10-28, computed on the 1 mM table only (40,324 rows). These answer
whether the floor should be stricter, and the answer is that the floor is not the binding filter.

Panel D -- the p-value is self-protecting where SF is not. Smallest p ANYWHERE in each bin:
  1-2: 1.5e-02 | 3-5: 5.1e-06 | 6-10: 1.1e-09 | 11-30: 2.5e-19
  31-100: 1.1e-31 | 101-300: 1.4e-37 | 301-1k: 8.5e-46 | >1k: 4.2e-49
At 1-2 reads NO row reaches q < 0.05 -- 0 of 8,818. A thin row can report SF = 1.000 and still
cannot reach significance, so the meta p-value already excludes what the SF artefact admits.
Rows reaching q < 0.05 by bin: 0 | 2.2 % | 6.2 % | 14.8 % | 36.1 % | 64.2 % | 87.6 % | 99.0 %.

Panel E -- the effective floor is 38 summed reads, not 10. Of 1,277 sites with q < 0.05 and
>= 3 passing replicates, the lowest-depth one carries 38 summed stall reads. G1 at 10 removes
nothing from the gated set; the replicate requirement is doing the filtering.

Cost of a stricter floor on the gated set (n = 1,277):
  >= 50: lose 4 (0.3 %) | >= 100: 25 (2.0 %) | >= 200: 65 (5.1 %) | >= 500: 169 (13.2 %)
The lost sites have HIGH median SF (0.839 at 50, 0.793 at 100), so a stricter floor removes the
high-SF thin sites specifically -- which is either the residual artefact or real strong elements
in poorly covered features, and this figure cannot separate the two.

UNRESOLVED, and the reason to keep looking. Among passing sites the median SF is NOT monotonic
in depth: 31-100: 0.763 | 101-300: 0.500 | 301-1k: 0.457 | >1k: 0.755. The bump at 31-100
(n = 26, the thinnest passing band) is what residual inflation would look like, and it is the
band a ~30-read candidate falls into. Either confirm it as inflation and raise the floor to 100,
or explain it. Do this before quoting SF for any site in that band.

CAVEAT on the depth measure. `stall_reads` here is SUMMED across replicates, matching
detectability_floor.py. The alternative is the best single replicate, which is more charitable
and is what zero_pass_wellpowered used. The two were reconciled in favour of best-tile for the
representation figure; for SF the summed count is the right denominator companion, but the choice
should be stated in the caption either way.
-->
